items.title: Walmart Just Dropped 10% in a Month. Is It Time to Sell?
items.summary: Walmart just posted a quarter where management raised its full-year outlook and e-commerce surged, yet shareholders watched the stock crater while a smaller rival celebrated a 13% gain. Something specific is spooking the market, and whether it signals a buying opportunity or a warning depends on one number.

items.title: What Could Lift Walmart Stock Is Not On Its Shelves
items.summary: The retailer keeps cutting shelf prices, and profit is growing far faster than the U.S. comp, with almost half of that growth coming from areas like advertising, marketplace, and membership.

items.title: Walmart’s Big Sell-Off Could Be a Buying Opportunity
items.summary: Walmart just punished investors for a beat-and-raise quarter, slicing 12% off shares in weeks. Before you follow the crowd out the door, consider what the selloff is actually pricing in.

items.title: Why Is Costco (COST) Refunding Tariff Duties While Fighting A Class Action?
items.summary: Costco Wholesale (NasdaqGS:COST) has begun refunding customers for unlawful duties collected on certain tariffed goods. The company is contesting a related class action lawsuit that challenges how those tariff related charges were handled. The refunds and legal dispute raise questions about future liabilities, customer relationships, and Costco's brand image. This kind of tariff and legal exposure is not unique to Costco.
